newsitem.title: FINLAND: MARKKA FLOAT OPTION IF FINLAND NOT IN EMU-TUOMIOJA.
newsitem.headline: MARKKA FLOAT OPTION IF FINLAND NOT IN EMU-TUOMIOJA.

text.p: Letting the markka float instead of pegging it to an ERM-II system should be considered as an option if Finland does not join the third stage of EMU in the first wave, the Social Democratic Party said on Tuesday.

SDP parliamentary group chairman Erkki Tuomioja told a parliament debate on the coalition government's EMU report that its view -- that the only realistic alternatives were joining EMU or linking to ERM-II -- should be reconsidered.
"If Finland ended up outside EMU, this choice must still be considered," he said.
"It is not self-evident that a floating (markka) would be a more susceptible alternative to the destructive effects of market forces," he said, but did not elaborate.

Tuomioja also said the government should reconsider a decision to bring the issue of Finnish EMU membership to parliament in the form of a notification. The cabinet should stand by its programme and bring a bill to parliament, he said.
Parliament will not vote on single currency membership at the end of the current debate on the report. The vote on participation is scheduled for early 1998.
Inside or outside monetary union, Finnish economic policy must in any case be targetted at stability and low inflation, Tuomioja said.
Outside EMU Finland would retain "very limited" room to manoeuvre in monetary and exchange rate policy, he said.
That leeway could be used in case of severe external economic disturbances, or to hold back the economy in times of very rapid growth, he said.
